name: Idaho

events.title: Statehood
events.text: Idaho became the 43rd state on July 3, 1890. Congress gave it 1 seat in the House until the next apportionment.

events.title: 1890 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1890 census, Idaho kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1900 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1900 census, Idaho kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1910 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1910 census, Idaho's House delegation grew from 1 to 2 seats.

events.title: Statewide (general ticket) elections
events.text: In the 63rd through 65th Congresses (1913–1919), Idaho elected all of its representatives statewide on a general ticket instead of by district.

events.title: 1930 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1930 census, Idaho kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1940 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1940 census, Idaho kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1950 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1950 census, Idaho kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1960 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1960 census, Idaho kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1970 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1970 census, Idaho kept 2 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1980 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1980 census, Idaho kept 2 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1990 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1990 census, Idaho kept 2 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Voters create redistricting commission
events.text: On November 8, 1994, Idaho voters approved SJR 105, a constitutional amendment moving congressional and legislative redistricting from the legislature to a six-member bipartisan commission. The commission adopted its first congressional plan on August 28, 2001.

events.title: 2000 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2000 census, Idaho kept 2 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Second commission after missed deadline
events.text: Idaho's first 2011 commission missed its September 6 deadline without adopting maps. A new commission was formed on September 13, 2011, and issued the congressional plan on October 17, 2011.

events.title: 2010 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2010 census, Idaho kept 2 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Pentico v. Denney
events.text: In the only court challenge to Idaho's 2021 congressional districts, the Idaho Supreme Court unanimously upheld the commission's map on February 11, 2022.

events.title: 2020 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2020 census, Idaho kept 2 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.

c066.text: Idaho's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1918 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c090.text: Idaho's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1966 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c093.text: New map drawn after the 1970 census, which left Idaho with 2 seats. It was first used in the 1972 election.
